lesson_title: Share, Swap or Sea: The Three Bonds That Build Everything
hook_text: Salt shatters. Copper bends. Same kind of building blocks — one tiny difference decides everything.
clip_script: Hit a salt crystal with a spoon and it shatters. Bend a copper wire and it just... bends. Both are giant grids of positive ions — so what is the difference? What sits in between. In salt, every plus ion is boxed in by minus ions: plus, minus, plus, minus, in strict order. Shift one layer a single step and suddenly plus faces plus. Attraction flips to repulsion and the crystal rips itself apart. That is why salt is brittle. In copper there are no fixed partners at all — just a sea of loose electrons washing around the positive ions, owned by everyone and no one. Push the layers and the sea simply flows around the new shape. The bond survives. The metal bends. And that same sea is why copper conducts: the charge is already free to move. Three bonds build the whole world: non-metals SHARE electron pairs and make molecules, metals and non-metals SWAP electrons and stack into grids, and metals alone pool everything into the sea. Share, swap, sea — and every property of every material starts making sense.
visual_style: A split screen: a salt lattice in crisp alternating colours that fractures along a glowing plane when layers shift, versus a copper lattice where a shimmering electron fluid flows around sliding ions; closing triptych labels the three bonds.
mood: Satisfying materials-science reveal with a clean punchline.
pacing: Sharp shatter opening, slow-motion lattice shift, fluid pour of the electron sea, crisp three-word summary landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to predict any material's personality from its bond.
